item.title: Lok Sabha passes anti-paper leak bill after row over Rahul's remarks
item.description: The Lok Sabha passed a bill to make paper leak punishments more stringent. This legislation aims to expedite trials and deter unfair means in public examinations. The bill proposes significant jail terms and hefty fines for individuals involved in paper leaks. Investigations into paper leak cases are to be completed within two months. The government also highlighted an increase in universities and higher education institutions.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Ahead of dengue vaccine rollout, all 4 strains found in circulation
item.description: India's first dengue virus mapping shows all four serotypes circulating in eight states. This finding could influence the country's upcoming dengue vaccine strategy. Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain across the nation. Concurrent infections with multiple strains are linked to more severe dengue disease. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for monitoring virus circulation and guiding policy.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: Continue with your duties fearlessly, CRPF chief tells troopers amid pellet gun row
item.description: CRPF Director General G P Singh supports troops acting in good faith during duty. He assures responsibility for all decisions made in the public interest. An internal probe found standard operating procedures were followed by RAF personnel. Pellet guns were used after other crowd dispersal methods failed. This investigation may prevent charges against the RAF personnel involved.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN

item.title: Murali Sreeshankar bags Silver in thrilling long jump final, misses Gold by 6 cm
item.description: Murali Sreeshankar secured the silver medal in the men's long jump event. He achieved a best leap of 8.09m in the fiercely contested final. Jamaica's Tajay Gayle won gold with a jump of 8.15m in the fourth round. Scotland's Stephen Mackenzie claimed the bronze medal with a jump of 8.08m. Lokesh finished fifth in his Commonwealth Games debut competition.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Amid opposition walkout, Rajya Sabha gives approval to Vande Mataram bill
item.description: The Rajya Sabha passed a bill proposing jail time for disrupting Vande Mataram. Opposition MPs walked out, demanding a statement on police action against protesters. Junior home minister Nityanand Rai piloted the bill, criticizing Congress's stance on the national song. MP Sanjay Singh questioned the RSS's past refusal to hoist the tricolour. AIADMK MPs noted the practice of playing state anthems after national songs.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: 'My mornings are for...': Jeff Bezos reveals he never makes any decisions before 10 am
item.description: Jeff Bezos prioritizes his mornings, dedicating this time to personal matters and family before diving into work. He strategically avoids challenging tasks until after 10 am, promoting a productive start to his day. He opts for critical conversations mid-morning when his mental clarity is at its peak. Research indicates that decision fatigue can hinder judgment, so Bezos emphasizes making a select number of high-quality decisions each day for maximum effectiveness.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Guard's accidental gunshot kills man visiting bank in city
item.description: A customer was killed Tuesday after a security guard's gun discharged accidentally. Manish Kumar, a farmer, was updating his Aadhaar card at the Union Bank branch. The ex-serviceman guard, Vinod Kumar, was loading cartridges when the firearm discharged. The bullet struck Manish in the back, and he was rushed to the hospital. Police have arrested the guard and are investigating the incident further.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: No ban on Jagannath movie, artists must enjoy creative liberty, says Supreme Court
item.description: The Supreme Court rejected a plea to ban an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath. Justices emphasized artists' creative expression and tolerance for depicting deities. They noted that preventing such depictions would halt many religious television programs. The court stated that the Censor Board's approval meant no judicial interference was needed. It refused to restrict artistic creativity based on the objections of a few.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: 'Iran is going to get a beating': Trump threatens 'hard' response after attack on US base
item.description: United States President Donald Trump warned Iran of a forceful military response. American bases in Jordan faced missile attacks which the US intercepted. Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility for the attempted surprise strike. US and Saudi forces also conducted overnight strikes against Iran-backed militias. Global markets reacted to the latest escalation in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: How Europe's heatwave is proving Americans right about air conditioning
item.description: Europeans are now buying air conditioning units in unprecedented numbers. Manufacturers report significant sales growth across several European countries. This shift is driven by both comfort and public health concerns. Rising temperatures and extreme heat events are becoming impossible to ignore. Cultural attitudes towards cooling solutions are beginning to change.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: PoK on the boil: Polls, a deadly crackdown by Pakistani forces and a region in turmoil
item.dc:creator: VIVEK DUBEY

item.title: Teen’s nuclear energy idea could cut Antarctic base emissions by 3,254 tons
item.description: A young Chilean student has proposed an innovative energy system for Antarctica. This concept combines renewable sources with a nuclear microreactor for reliable power. The system aims to significantly reduce diesel fuel dependence and carbon emissions. It offers a potential solution for powering remote research stations in extreme conditions. This student-led idea highlights future possibilities for sustainable Antarctic energy.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: El Salvador burial under 2,800-year ash held turtle-shaped vessel
item.description: Archaeologists discovered a 2,800-year-old burial in El Salvador clutching a sea turtle vessel. This Mesoamerican burial may belong to a pre-Maya civilization which practiced human sacrifice. The skeleton was found under volcanic ash from an eruption dating to 850-830 BC. Cassava remnants found in the pit symbolize continuation and spiritual resonance. Further chemical analysis will reveal more about the individual's life and diet.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: JPMorgan CEO recalls his Citigroup firing: Shares meeting with mentor Sandy Weill
item.description: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon discussed two major life events. His 1998 Citigroup dismissal reshaped his career path significantly. His youngest daughter asked if the family would now have to “sleep on the streets”. A near-fatal heart emergency in 2020 brought him peace. Dimon invested heavily in Bank One after leaving Citigroup. This bold move led to his leadership at JPMorgan Chase.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Indian Embassy in US slams foreign media for misleading headline over PoK killings
item.description: The Indian Embassy criticized The New York Times for its inaccurate reporting. The embassy stated Pakistan illegally occupies parts of Jammu and Kashmir. Violent clashes have occurred in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir since early June. Protests are ongoing over regional legislative assembly seats and alleged manipulation. India attributes these protests to Pakistan's economic exploitation and oppression.
item.dc:creator: TOI NEWS DESK

item.title: D4vd eligible for death penalty as prosecutors review Celeste Rivas murder case
item.description: Singer D4vd, David Anthony Burke, faces potential death penalty charges. Prosecutors are weighing the death penalty for the murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Burke has pleaded not guilty to all serious charges against him. The case moves forward after a judge found sufficient evidence for trial. His next court hearing is scheduled for August 31 in Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: SUMIT ROY

item.title: Lamine Yamal says his mother's sacrifices outweigh childhood struggles he endured
item.description: Lamine Yamal, the 19-year-old World Cup winner, has spoken openly about a childhood shaped by financial hardship and parental sacrifice. His mother, Sheila Ebana, emigrated from Equatorial Guinea to Spain as a teenager, had Yamal at 16, and raised him largely alone after separating from his father when Lamine was three. Yamal credits her with shielding him from the worst of their circumstances, saying she made him see only the beautiful side of life. He also reflected on his rapid rise at Barcelona, describing himself as a creative and entertaining player who never anticipated reaching the first team quite so quickly
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Kings linked with Patrik Laine as bold signing prediction gains momentum
item.description: The Los Angeles Kings are said to be keen on adding forward Patrik Laine to their roster. This move aims to enhance their offensive prowess, as NHL analysts have frequently connected Laine with the Kings. His exceptional scoring ability and power play skills could significantly benefit the team. Acquiring Laine might be a strategic risk worth taking as they prepare for the season ahead.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Nolan Wells' family seeks social media records amid missing phone data concerns
item.description: Nolan Wells’ family has subpoenaed several social media companies as investigators continue examining the 18-year-old’s death. The requests focus on account records and digital data after the family raised concerns about missing Snapchat content on Wells’ phone. His friend Warren Hudson has denied that anyone accessed or deleted information from the device. The investigation remains ongoing.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Paredes faces 3 assault charges; FIFA charges Argentina over 'Malvinas' banner
item.description: FIFA initiated disciplinary proceedings against Argentina players and officials. Charges include assault allegations and unsporting behaviour after the World Cup final. The Argentine Football Association faces accusations for fan conduct and political demonstrations. Players and staff may receive match suspensions and financial penalties for their actions. FIFA will review all submissions before announcing its final verdict.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Why mosquitoes are choosing human blood more often, according to scientists
item.description: Scientists observed mosquitoes in Brazil's Atlantic Forest feeding on humans more often. This shift suggests habitat loss is pushing mosquitoes towards human hosts. DNA analysis revealed this surprising feeding pattern in protected forest areas. Disappearing wildlife populations may force mosquitoes to seek new blood sources. Protecting forests could help reduce future risks from mosquito-borne diseases.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Sanjeev Kumar predicted his early death, says Sachin Pilgaonkar on final days
item.description: Sachin Pilgaonkar recounted his missed final meeting with close friend Sanjeev Kumar. He arrived at Sanjeev Kumar's residence later than planned that fateful afternoon. Colleagues reflected on Sanjeev Kumar's demanding work and lifestyle choices. His fascination with playing older characters stemmed from a palm reader's prediction. Sanjeev Kumar passed away prematurely at the age of forty-seven.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Horoscope today: Daily astrological predictions for Thursday
item.description: Horoscope Today: Read daily horoscope predictions for July 30, 2026. Know all about the astrological events and influences that will be affecting each of the 12 zodiac signs. Our astrologer has analyzed the movements of the planets and the alignment of the stars to bring you the most accurate and up-to-date horoscope predictions for the day ahead. Get ready to discover what the stars have in store for you today.
item.dc:creator: SAMIR JAIN

item.title: J&K politicians urge UN, PM Modi to intervene over PoK killings
item.description: Political parties in Jammu and Kashmir are urging intervention over alleged killings. Over two dozen people were reportedly killed in firing by Pakistani security forces. National Conference president Farooq Abdullah called for a UN Human Rights Council team. CPM legislator MY Tarigami demanded an end to force and an inquiry. Unrest has escalated in PoK after authorities banned the Joint Awami Action Committee.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: How Savannah James built a thriving business empire beyond LeBron James' fame
item.description: Savannah James has built a successful career through business, interior design, philanthropy, and community leadership. From launching furniture projects to mentoring young women and working with respected brands, she has created her own identity beyond basketball. While supporting her family, she has continued growing as an entrepreneur, proving that her achievements extend far beyond being LeBron James’ wife.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: US Federal Reserve meet today: Kevin Warsh-led FOMC keeps interest rates unchanged
item.description: The US Federal Reserve, which began its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday, was widely expected to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Schools closed in Kishtwar, Doda amid inclement weather
item.description: Authorities ordered school closures in Doda and Kishtwar districts due to inclement weather. The Amarnath pilgrimage continued solely on the Baltal route with many devotees. Vaishno Devi yatra also proceeded but only via the traditional Ardhkuwari track. The Jammu-Srinagar national highway remained open for all vehicular traffic. The IMD predicted continued rain and potential flash floods across the region.
item.dc:creator: SANJAY KHAJURIA

item.title: Tourists no longer sleep in taxis, Farooq Abdullah hails hotel boom in Kashmir
item.description: In a recent statement, LG Manoj Sinha commended hotels for their role as facilitators of peace and their significant financial commitments to the sector. He pointed out that numerous hotels had overlooked crucial construction regulations. Farooq Abdullah highlighted the employment opportunities generated by hotels, reminiscing about a time when accommodation options were limited.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: MP farmers breach barricades, reach within 1 km of CM Mohan Yadav's residence over moong MSP
item.description: Farmers in Bhopal protested over summer moong procurement at minimum support price. They breached police barricades and marched towards the Chief Minister's residence. The state government formed a committee to discuss issues with farmer representatives. Talks between the agriculture minister and farmer leaders concluded without a breakthrough. The protest continued with various demonstrations and roadside activities.
item.dc:creator: AYUSH PANDEY

item.title: Watch: Terrifying one-punch knockout at CWG leaves boxer hanging through ropes
item.description: Orlando Holley-Sotomi of Wales delivered a powerful knockout during the Commonwealth Games boxing quarterfinal. His opponent, Refiloe Thai, was sent through the ropes after a devastating right hand landed. Medical staff quickly attended to the injured boxer, who thankfully showed signs of recovery. This victory guarantees Holley-Sotomi at least a bronze medal in the competition.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Hyderabad: Trainee IPS officer arrested for sexual harassment of co-trainee
item.description: A trainee IPS officer was arrested for allegedly harassing a woman co-trainee. The accused faces charges of stalking and sexual harassment at the police academy. He reportedly sent abusive messages and made derogatory remarks to the complainant. The woman also alleged physical assault and blackmail attempts by the officer. Police registered a case under relevant sections of the law.
item.dc:creator: TOI CITY DESK

item.title: 'Like losing the woman of your life': Mancini apologises after dramatic Italy return
item.description: Roberto Mancini has apologised for his previous departure from the Italian national team. He admitted his exit was completely his fault and expressed deep regret. Mancini returns as Italy's coach after their World Cup qualification failures. He aims to restore the Azzurri to their former glory and win back trust. The team's new era begins with a UEFA Nations League match.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Relief for automakers as Centre proposes easy easing emission compliance testing regime
item.description: The road transport ministry proposes changes to emission compliance testing for vehicle manufacturers. New passenger cars and two-wheelers will undergo annual testing for three years after approval. Larger vehicles will continue with annual emission compliance testing. Existing models will see testing frequency reduced to once every three years. This move aims to reduce compliance burdens and improve ease of doing business.
item.dc:creator: DIPAK K DASH

item.title: Kanpur man kills wife, applies sindoor on her head before hanging self
item.description: In a tragic incident in Kanpur, a newly married couple, Saurabh Savita and Shalini, were found dead in their rented room. Police speculate that Saurabh may have strangled Shalini before taking his own life, applying vermilion, a symbol of marital status. Their court marriage, done in secrecy without familial approval, had caused considerable tension within their families. Investigations are ongoing to uncover the motive behind this heartbreaking situation.
item.dc:creator: FAIZ RAHMAN SIDDIQUI

item.title: Meta tells IT ministry PM Modi's posts will get additional oversight, senior reviews
item.description: Meta assured the government of enhanced oversight for Prime Minister Modi's posts. This assurance followed the brief removal of his video addressing the NEET paper leak issue. The company admitted the video's temporary removal was due to an unintended error. Prime Minister Modi had discussed stricter measures against paper leaks in the video. Meta officials will meet government representatives soon to discuss this incident further.
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: Neymar confirms Brazil retirement: 'My time with the national team is over'
item.description: Neymar has officially confirmed his retirement from international football after a long career. His decision follows Brazil's recent exit from the FIFA World Cup tournament. The veteran forward ends his international journey with numerous goals and assists. He also addressed and dismissed recent dressing-room criticism reports. Neymar helped Santos secure a victory in the Copa Sudamericana match.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Inside US-Saudi nuclear deal: Why Pakistan is biggest loser
item.description: The newly forged nuclear pact between the US and Saudi Arabia promises to transform the atomic dynamics in the region. This agreement grants Saudi Arabia the ability to enrich uranium domestically, supervised by the United States, effectively diminishing Pakistan's nuclear dominance. The emergence of a nuclear triangle comprising Israel, Iran, and Saudi Arabia signals a significant shift in U.S. non-proliferation efforts, embracing a tiered regional order.
item.dc:creator: AASHISH SAXENA

item.title: Rahul's 'advice' to PM Modi, and 3 guarantees to students over police action on protesters
item.description: Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of denying him Lok Sabha speech rights. He refused to apologize for blaming Amit Shah for police brutality. Gandhi demanded the Home Minister's dismissal and an independent probe. He alleged police used pellet guns and nail-fitted lathis on students. Gandhi promised justice and accountability for the injured students.
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: What India needs to do amid emerging global challenges: Finance ministry outlines
item.description: The report stressed that deeper domestic reforms and quicker policy execution will be essential to alter the country's long-term economic trajectory.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: India-US trade pact: Piyush Goyal explains the one condition to seal the deal
item.description: India's trade pact with the US awaits tariff competitiveness restoration for its first phase. Minister Piyush Goyal stated India needs a comparative advantage over rival nations. This condition must be met before the bilateral trade agreement can commence. Meanwhile, a US legislative proposal could impose tariffs on Russian energy buyers. India has increased its Russian crude oil purchases amid supply disruptions.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Five wins, nine medals assured! Indian boxers deliver flawless day at CWG 2026
item.description: The Commonwealth Games witnessed India's boxing squad achieving an impressive milestone by winning all five matches. Five Indian athletes have now made it to the semifinals, guaranteeing at least nine bronze medals for the country. Sakshi Choudhary and Arundhati Choudhary kick-started the victory parade with their bouts, complemented by the triumphs of Sachin Siwach, Ankush Yadav, and Narender Berwal.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Varanasi: Man stabs live-in partner to death after drunken fight over washing utensils
item.description: A live-in relationship between two gay partners in Varanasi ended tragically on Monday night. One partner, Kush Pandey, fatally stabbed his live-in partner, Dipanshu Rai, during a quarrel. The dispute reportedly began over washing dishes after consuming alcohol together. Police arrested Kush Pandey at the scene and sent Dipanshu Rai's body for postmortem. The couple had been living together for a year and often argued after drinking.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV DIKSHIT
